prompt: On a summer night in a Ming Dynasty royal bedchamber, the candlelight is dim in the room. an emperor lies wearily on an ornately carved dragon-and-phoenix canopy bed, barely mustering the energy to adjust his golden brocade quilt. His simple yet elegant imperial yellow silk night robe--adorned with faint golden dragon motifs--clings lightly to his frame, emphasizing a gaunt silhouette from prolonged fatigue. The room is dimly lit by a flickering oil lamp on a cluttered nightstand, beside which rest unrolled official memorials with 朱砂批阅 (vermilion annotations), an inkstone still wet with fresh ink, and a disheveled wolf-hair brush. Moonlight streams through lattice windows, casting sharp shadows on his hollowed cheeks and the stack of unresolved documents teetering at the bedside. A half-drunk cup of cold tea sits on a weathered wooden tray, its surface dotted with mosquito larvae, while a neglected brazier emits dying embers, symbolizing the late hour. The bed’s elaborate carvings contrast starkly with the emperor’s exhausted posture, and a sheer mosquito netting hangs askew, untouched in the rush of late-night duties. Outside, the palace courtyard lies silent, save for the distant toll of a water clock marking the third watch.
